title: Updater Services Ltd - 543996 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Updater Services FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR2,960 crores, but adjusted EBITDA margin was 5.9% after the Avon provisioning hit; no formal FY27 guidance given.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 3% YoY to INR750 crores and EBITDA was INR49 crores (6.6% margin), with PAT of INR27 crores. For FY26, IFM grew 10% to INR1,995 crores and BSS grew 1% to INR966 crores, while adjusted EBITDA was INR176 crores after absorbing the Avon receivables provision of about INR23 crores. Management said standalone UDS PAT fell on front-loaded IFM costs, provisions, lower interest income and a one-time wage-code charge, and framed FY27 as a clean year. Management declined formal FY27 guidance and said acquisition talks are still live but not assured.

financial_highlights.change: +3% YoY (vs INR726 crores in Q4 FY25)

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 adjusted EBITDA (after Avon one-time hit)

financial_highlights.value: INR966 crores, EBITDA margin 8.8% (adjusted INR85 crores EBITDA per Amitabh, ~9%)

segments.name: IFM
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,995 crores (+10% YoY), EBITDA margin 4.5%; Global Flight Handling EBITDA rose to 6% from 3%, Fusion margin ~6% to ~8%, Washroom Hygiene margin steady at 37-38%. Management says IFM growth is ahead of peers.

segments.name: BSS - Denave
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR590 crores (+11% YoY), EBITDA INR26 crores (~4.5% margin); Q4 revenue +15% and EBITDA +~70% with margin 5.5%+. Added 49 new logos; new and existing enterprise business grew 21%.

segments.name: BSS - Athena
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR116.8 crores vs INR136 crores in FY25; EBITDA INR23-24 crores vs INR35 crores, margin ~20-21%. BFSI concentration fell to 81% from 86%; 4 new logos added, no new customer losses in FY26.

segments.name: BSS - Matrix
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR128.6 crores; EBGC (background verification) revenue fell 11% on IT/ITES hiring softness, Audit & Assurance grew 5.8%. EBITDA INR14.9-15 crores, margin ~12%.

segments.name: Avon
segments.commentary: Avon took about INR23 crores of provisions (INR3 crores in Q2, balance in Q3) on logistics and freight brokerage receivables, fully provided; legal action underway. Core mail room and integrated support business grew 9%. Avon Transport has been shut.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance; management expects to grow ahead of the Indian industry (industry grew under 6% in FY26).
Management expects a clean FY27 start, with the one-time wage-code, front-loaded cost and provisioning items not repeating.
Visibility on FY27 revenue of 85-90% from existing contracts, per management.
Management said it hopes to indicate the FY27 year-end direction on the Q1 FY27 call.
Early April-May signs are encouraging, and several large IFM logos are signed or pending approval.
capex_capacity: All 23 Global Flight Handling airports are now operational and generating revenue.
Denave is scaling AI-led digital workforce pilots, which were run with 4 customers in FY26, and plans to scale them meaningfully in FY27.
Athena is in POC stages on agentic AI with 3-4 customers and won 2 Agentic AI contracts recently.
Management said it will invest in technology and AI, and talent, from its cash pool.
Shared services across finance, procurement and payroll are planned to drive cost optimisation.
demand_pricing: IFM: 30 new logos added in FY26 across industrial, technology and commercial sectors, with higher wallet share from existing clients.
Management cites demand tailwinds from the new labour codes (effective November 2025), GCC growth and outcome-linked contracts.
Matrix A&A won 12 large clients across FMCG, retail, quick commerce and manufacturing; one large customer reduced spend.
EBGC demand is soft due to IT and ITES hiring and some softness in BFSI hiring.
Athena: losses of 2 major customers and a downsizing by another in FY25 and earlier drove the revenue decline; diversifying into healthcare, retail and real estate.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~INR450 crore cash pile be deployed, including acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said acquisitions remain the primary use, alongside organic investment in technology and talent and shareholder rewards. The Board will decide the split, and some form of reward is expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there early recovery at Athena, and what is the steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Major customer losses have stopped; EBITDA margin has stabilised at about 19-20%. Key priorities are customer diversification and scaling agentic AI, which is at POC stage with 3-4 customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BSS revenue fall sharply and margins rise, and what drove IFM's PAT decline and the other opex drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Athena revenue fell about INR25 crores and Avon Transport (INR40 crores last year) was shut. Denave grew 11%, Global 30%, Avon Solutions 11%, and Matrix was flat. Standalone UDS PAT fell about INR19 crores: roughly INR12-13 crores from front-loaded costs and ECL/EPC provisions, INR4 crores from wage-code liabilities, and the rest from lower interest income, after a INR9 crore non-operating gain last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is returns on capital low despite revenue growth, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IFM growth is ahead of peers (IFM +10%, group +7%). It attributed the margin drop to one-time items that will not repeat and said interest income is a capital-allocation outcome that will rise with treasury management.

qa_highlights.question: Why no buyback given the net cash position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash is earmarked for organic growth, acquisitions and shareholder rewards, with the format (buyback or dividend) to be a Board decision and some reward expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY27 revenue is already visible, and what is the FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Visibility is 85-90% from existing contracts. Management declined formal guidance and expects to give an indication on the Q1 FY27 call.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the pending acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: The deal is still on; due diligence is almost closed, but other negotiating items remain and completion cannot be guaranteed. Management is cautiously hopeful.

risks_watch: Avon receivables recovery: about INR23 crores fully provided, with legal action underway; any recovery would be upside.
IFM margin: segment EBITDA margin was 4.4% in Q4 and 4.5% for FY26; front-loaded contract costs need to unwind as management expects.
Athena revenue continues to shrink, and the agentic AI POCs have not yet converted to scaled revenue.
EBGC/Matrix is exposed to IT, ITES and BFSI hiring softness.
Acquisition outcome is uncertain, and cash deployment (M&A vs buyback vs dividend) is undecided.
Management reported a decline in standalone PAT in FY26 and is expecting a clean FY27, which should be verified against Q1 FY27 results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on structural tailwinds and cash generation, but cautious and non-committal on FY27 numbers, declining formal guidance and deferring to the Q1 call. Management was candid on the Avon provisions and the standalone PAT decline, and attributed them to one-time items.
key_quotes: We're taking all necessary steps, including legal action to recover these amounts.
Being prudent and conservative, we have already fully provided for the entire INR23 crores.
I would avoid a formal guidance in terms of where we are going to go.
So it is still on. The conversations have taken longer than what we had envisaged.
